_meta.description: 2026-07-18 Q&A-engine rebuild: agents now ask real questions directly to Claude (data-center) or Gemini (a specific Notebook-X notebook) — see CLAUDE.md and workers/qa-engine.js. The old per-day CALL-COUNT Claude cap (claude_daily_cap, removed below) is retired in favor of a single shared DOLLAR budget (shared_claude_budget below) tracked in D1's claude_budget_usage table (workers/model-router.js) — the SAME table the chore-automation economy already used, not a new separate one. Routine persona flavor (coworker chat, follow-up phrasing, AI-experience notes, critiques) runs Groq-first with Cloudflare fallback via agent-base.js queryGroqRouted() (renamed 2026-07-19 from the misleadingly-named queryGemini()); Hebrew/bilingual composition (gap notes, Trainee guides) goes direct to Gemini via queryGeminiDirect(), meeting-engine report synthesis calls callGemini() itself, and Notebook-X asks also go direct to Gemini, paced by workers/gemini-pacer.js. Agent 10 (Architect) is dormant — excluded from this flow entirely, not just from routine cases.

_app_search_model_meta: Corrected from the stale 'claude-sonnet-4-6' claim (Guides-feature session) — the owner verified directly that data-center-api runs Sonnet 5 today. This field is documentation only (data-center-api chooses its own model independently); workers/claude-client.js's CLAUDE_MODEL constant, used by the Guides pipeline's own direct Anthropic calls, is the actual source of truth for that pipeline and is set to the same 'claude-sonnet-5'.

shared_claude_budget._meta: Added 2026-07-18, replaces the retired claude_daily_cap (a per-day CALL COUNT, checked against `interactions` rows). This is a per-MONTH DOLLAR cap, checked/recorded via workers/model-router.js's getClaudeBudgetStatus()/recordClaudeSpend() — the exact same D1 claude_budget_usage table and functions the chore-automation economy already used (see chore_automation.claude_budget_usd_per_month below, now the single source of truth for this cap; briefly bumped 4.50 -> 5.00 on 2026-07-18 when the budgets were unified, then restored to 4.50 later that day as a deliberate soft-stop leaving real headroom under the account's own $5/month spend ceiling — the two numbers are distinct mechanisms, software soft-stop vs account hard limit). 'Shared' is not aspirational — office-agent Q&A Claude calls (agents/agent-base.js _askDataCenter()) and chore-automation Claude calls (workers/chore-runner.js) draw from and record against the SAME month row, by design, per this session's explicit instruction not to create a second budget.
shared_claude_budget._max_calls_per_day_meta: Added 2026-07-19 (owner-approved rebalance): hard per-day Claude CALL cap — calls, not questions, so follow-up asks count too. Enforced at BOTH layers: (a) generation time — workers/qa-engine.js generateAssignedDailyBatch() assigns at most this many data-center-targeted questions per generation call (one call per simulated day), overflow re-picked from the notebook-x pool; (b) ask time — agents/agent-base.js _askDataCenter() skips (logged, tool_used 'claude-daily-cap-skip') once today's interactions rows with model_source='claude' reach this count (model-router.js getClaudeCallsToday(), UTC calendar day per this repo's DATE('now') convention — a simulated Israel day spans two UTC dates at the 23:00Z first batch, so the effective worst case is ~cap+first-batch, still well under the monthly soft-stop). Worst case 10 x ~$0.0101 x 31d ~= $3.13/mo vs the $4.50 soft-stop. NOT the same mechanism as the retired claude_daily_cap (30, which gated ALL agent Claude usage before the dollar budget existed); this is a routing-mix control layered UNDER the monthly dollar cap, not a replacement for it.

graduated_rollout_throttle._meta: Added 2026-07-18 for the FIRST LIVE ACTIVATION of the Q&A engine (cron re-enabled the same day, first run 2026-07-19). This is a TEMPORARY graduated-rollout throttle, NOT a permanent volume limit: workers/agent-runner.js's computeDailyQuestionVolume() caps the day's generated question total at ramp_daily_caps[N], where N = calendar days elapsed in Israel time since activation_date_israel (N=0 on the activation day itself). Once N >= ramp_daily_caps.length the throttle is automatically inert — volume returns to the normal budget-driven computation with NO manual step-up needed. The per-call $-budget check (_askDataCenter) and Gemini pacing (gemini-pacer.js) remain the real backstops throughout. Safe to delete this whole block once the ramp window has passed; applyGraduatedRolloutCap() treats a missing block as 'no throttle'.

guides_claude_budget._meta: Added for the Guides feature (workers/guide-engine.js): a SECOND, independent Claude sub-budget alongside shared_claude_budget above — total Anthropic spend rises $5 -> $10/month, split into two $5 sub-budgets each with its own $4.50 soft-stop (matching shared_claude_budget's own headroom convention under the account's real spend ceiling, now effectively $10/month combined). Tracked via the SAME D1 claude_budget_usage table and the SAME workers/model-router.js getClaudeBudgetStatus()/recordClaudeSpend() functions as shared_claude_budget, distinguished by an explicit component:'guides' option (default is 'qa', so every pre-existing caller is untouched) and a distinct month key ('YYYY-MM#guides' vs 'YYYY-MM') — overrun in one sub-budget cannot drain the other. Covers: the Architect's (agent 10) review/finalize pass on each daily draft (workers/claude-client.js, direct Anthropic API, model claude-sonnet-5) plus the weekly Saturday verification pass (same model, +web_search tool). Fail-by-skip on exhaustion, logged, mirroring the existing 'claude-budget-skip' pattern — occasional skipped guide days are expected and acceptable, per the owner's cost approval (one review pass ~=$0.06-0.085/guide, one-revision worst case ~=$0.12-0.17, ~1 guide/day expected $2.50-3.50/month, all-revisions worst case ~=$5.30/month which DOES breach this soft-stop by design — the skip mechanism is load-bearing here, not decorative).

notebook_x_gemini_pacing._meta: Added 2026-07-18. See workers/gemini-pacer.js's header comment for the full reasoning — summary here for anyone reading this config without the code.
notebook_x_gemini_pacing.why_not_a_precise_quota_split: Gemini's free-tier per-minute quota is shared across THREE consumers this repo cannot fully observe: Notebook-X's own backend (live /ask traffic + its weekly gap-analysis job), this office Q&A automation, and other existing Gemini usage in office-AI-agents itself (report synthesis, coworker chat, gap-report composition). With two of the three consumers invisible to this repo, computing an exact 'fair share' would be false precision — the only safe posture is conservative, wide spacing from THIS automation, leaving deliberate headroom rather than trying to use a computed maximum.
notebook_x_gemini_pacing.mechanism: skip-if-too-soon via a KV-tracked last-call timestamp, not an in-Worker blocking sleep — see checkGeminiPacingSlot().

description: Groq and CF AI are free — run agents hard. Claude is paid — capped by shared_claude_budget above ($4.50/month soft-stop shared with chore-automation, under the account's own $5/month spend ceiling), not a per-day call count. Primary purpose: real usage of both production AI systems (Claude, Gemini) surfaces genuine capability gaps.

_meta.description: Per-provider FREE-TIER limits for the task-type routing table (workers/model-router.js, plan Phase 3). Every provider client module added this session (workers/github-models-client.js, cerebras-client.js, mistral-client.js, cohere-client.js) exports a matching `<PROVIDER>_LIMITS` constant, and scripts/verify-providers.js asserts this block and those constants agree — so changing one alone FAILS the verifier instead of drifting silently. Code and config are two copies of the same fact here on purpose: the client modules deliberately import no JSON, so they can be loaded by a plain `node` verifier.
_meta.the_overtime_rule: EVERY PROVIDER IN THIS BLOCK STAYS ON ITS FREE TIER. `paid: false` is a standing constraint, not a current observation. Any paid usage anywhere — a new provider, an upgraded plan, or an overage on an existing one — requires the owner's EXPLICIT, PER-INSTANCE approval, called 'overtime'. It is never a standing budget and never a monthly allowance: one approval, one instance, asked for at the time. A session or code path that needs paid usage STOPS AND ASKS; it does not spend and report. There is no automatic escalation from a free tier to a paid one, for any provider, ever — a call that would exceed a free tier is refused and logged as `overtime_required`.
_meta.anthropic_is_deliberately_absent: Anthropic does NOT appear in this block, and its absence is load-bearing rather than an omission. This block enumerates providers the ROUTER may select, and Anthropic is never routed and never shuffled — it is reserved for the Architect and genuine data-center Q&A, under the separate shared_claude_budget / guides_claude_budget caps above. Its two live call paths (agents/agent-base.js _askDataCenter() via the APP_API service binding, and workers/claude-client.js's direct Messages API calls for the Guides pipeline) are pre-existing DIRECT callers that never went through the router and are untouched by it. scripts/verify-providers.js asserts no anthropic key exists here.
_meta.nulls_are_honest: A null limit means THIS REPO DOES NOT KNOW the number — it does not mean unlimited. Where a real free-tier figure was not established against the live provider this session, it is null with a note rather than a plausible-looking invention, because a cap the router enforces against a number nobody verified is worse than no local cap at all: it refuses real work for a reason that was never true. The router treats null as 'pace conservatively and believe the response headers'. The supervised test procedure (back-office-AI-agents/docs/procedures/) establishes the real values against live APIs before any lane carries volume.
_meta.pre_existing_providers: groq / cloudflare_ai / gemini were already in service before this block existed. `daily_limits` above REMAINS the source of truth for their daily numbers; they are repeated here only so the router sees one uniform provider shape, and verify-providers.js asserts the two agree.

github_models.role: Judgment / quality lane PRIMARY — short scored calls (QA, Lead QA, Team Lead reviews).
github_models._token_caps_note: The ~8K input / ~4K output per-request caps are the defining constraint of this lane: they make it RIGHT for short judgment calls and WRONG for long report processing, which goes to cerebras. The client module REFUSES oversized input rather than truncating it, and refuses an over-cap output request rather than clamping it — see its header for why truncation specifically is forbidden in this repo (the 2026-07-11/12 incident).
github_models._rate_null_note: requests_per_minute / requests_per_day are null because GitHub Models publishes DIFFERENT request-rate allowances per model tier — there is no single honest number for this field. Read the real allowance for the configured model at supervised-test time.
github_models._secret_scope_note: Deliberately its own secret, NOT a reuse of the existing GITHUB_TOKEN. That token carries repo WRITE scope for report/guide commits; giving it to an inference path would hand a model-calling code path more reach than its work requires — exactly what the one-scoped-token-per-target decision (plan item 0.8) exists to prevent.

cerebras.role: Long-document lane PRIMARY (daily report batches) + judgment lane BACKUP.
cerebras._null_note: UNCOMFORTABLE BUT HONEST: the context ceiling is null on the provider whose entire job is long input. The free-tier context limit here varies by model and has moved before, and no live call was made this session to establish today's value. Establishing it is the FIRST item in this lane's supervised test — until then the only protection against an over-long request is the provider's own 400, surfaced as a logged null.

mistral.role: BACKUP only, in two lanes — long-document (behind cerebras) and Hebrew composition (behind gemini). Primary in none.
mistral._hebrew_note: Its Hebrew-composition role is the one carrying real quality risk: Hebrew internal notes are the office's own voice, Gemini is primary there for a reason, and this runs when Gemini is exhausted or paced out. A weaker Hebrew note still beats a skipped one — but the gap is precisely what the Lead QA's cross-embodiment comparison exists to measure, so it gets measured, not assumed. The Front is ENGLISH ONLY, so this lane never touches published content.

cohere.role: Embeddings / semantic search ONLY — never chat, not even as a backup. This lane has NO backup by design.
cohere._no_backup_note: 'Fail, don't degrade' is a CORRECTNESS rule here, not a preference. Vectors from two different embedding models do not share a space, so a similarity score computed across them is meaningless — and meaningless in the worst way, since it still returns a confident-looking number between 0 and 1. Substituting a backup provider would corrupt a search index rather than slow it down.
cohere._no_callers_yet_note: EXPECTED to have zero callers for some time. It exists for two capabilities that are designed but NOT BUILT: the local brain's semantic search over campus/agents/<NN-slug>/adaptations/, and the Lead QA's cross-report comparison (plan items 2.7 and 1.5). It ships now because it ships on the one set of secrets the owner installs once.

groq.role: Routine volume lane PRIMARY (drafts, worker chatter) + classification lane BACKUP. Pre-existing.
groq._source: daily_limits.groq / groq_reset_utc above remain the source of truth; repeated here for a uniform provider shape.

cloudflare_ai.role: Classification / routing lane PRIMARY + routine volume lane BACKUP. Pre-existing; account-scoped AI binding, no secret.
cloudflare_ai._source: daily_limits.cloudflare_ai / cloudflare_fallback above remain the source of truth.

gemini.role: Hebrew composition lane PRIMARY (gap notes, summaries) + report synthesis + Notebook-X asks. Pre-existing.
gemini._source: daily_limits.gemini / gemini_reset_israel / notebook_x_gemini_pacing above remain the source of truth.
gemini._pacing_note: Gemini's free-tier quota is shared with consumers this repo cannot observe (Notebook-X's own backend and its weekly gap-analysis job). workers/gemini-pacer.js's 20s spacing STAYS IN FORCE under routing — routing does not get to spend the headroom that pacing deliberately leaves.
